answer:
Zero-noise extrapolation raised the noisy answer from 0.198 to 0.228. A perfect machine would give 0.244, so the method closed about two thirds of the gap.

What I built: a line of 6 spins, all pointing up at the start, evolved to time 1 under H = (sum of ZZ on neighbors) + (sum of X). The circuit has 4 second-order Trotter steps. On Garnet's native gates it is 40 CZ gates, using qubits 8, 3, 4, 9, 10, 5. I made two stretched copies by global gate folding. The x3 copy is U, then U undone, then U again (120 CZ). The x5 copy repeats that once more (200 CZ). Barriers stop the compiler from cancelling the extra gates. All three copies have the same ideal answer, but they collect 1, 3 and 5 times the noise.

Job check: I submitted all 3 circuits as one job to garnet:mock, 1000 shots each. Job 01a16043-4021-7131-96b9-46f2e3138e80 completed and cost 0 credits. The mock only checks that the job is valid. Its counts are placeholders that do not depend on the circuit, so I did not use them for physics.

Noisy values: I ran the same 3 compiled circuits on IQMFakeGarnet, IQM's noisy simulator of Garnet, with 50,000 shots each. Magnetization is the average of Z over the 6 spins.
- Noise x1: 0.198
- Noise x3: 0.150
- Noise x5: 0.118

The value falls as noise grows, because noise pushes the spins toward random, which is magnetization 0.

Extrapolation: I fit a parabola through the 3 points (Richardson extrapolation) and read it at noise 0. That gives 0.228. A straight-line fit gives 0.215. The perfect answer for this circuit, from a noiseless statevector, is 0.244. The error dropped from 0.046 (raw) to 0.016 (mitigated).

A side note: the exact continuous-time physics gives 0.204. The 0.04 difference from 0.244 comes from cutting time into 4 steps. It is not machine noise, and ZNE cannot remove it.

The principle: you cannot switch the noise off, but you can turn it up on purpose. If you measure how the answer changes as noise grows, you can extend that trend back to zero noise. That trick is how IBM's 2023 experiment got useful numbers from a noisy processor.
